In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-culture system is a valuable tool to study AChE and its interactions with agrin and the neuromuscle junction.
AChE and/or agrin are important for NMJ development, but that their precise functions and the underlying mechanisms are still poorly understood.
AChE and/or agrin are involved in a variety of processes in skeletal muscle, including myogenesis, muscle differentiation and regeneration, and myofiber maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AChE is an important regulator of human skeletal muscle development and that agrin is involved in myoblast fusion and muscle cell differentiation.
the co-culture model is highly useful to study AChE and/or agrin in human muscle and that the results obtained in co-culture can be interpreted with the help of other experimental models.

The main takeaway from our work is that

AChE and, in particular, agrin play key roles in the development of human skeletal muscle and its innervation, and that their alternative functions in skeletal muscle may be related to the control of muscle growth and regeneration.
